title: Smoky kale crisps with pumpkin seeds

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Kale, olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, pumpkin seeds and hard cheese are all whole, ordinary foods with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday Tesco item at a normal price, including the vegetarian hard cheese and pumpkin seeds.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only two roasting trays, a bowl, a tea towel and a grater, and the technique is simple.

works.reason: 200g kale at 140C fan for 15 to 20 minutes, spread over two trays, gives a sensible snack for four that crisps without burning.

honest_times.reason: Stripping, washing, drying and oiling 200g of kale fits in 15 minutes, and preheating, baking and resting add up to about 35 minutes.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Frost-sweetened December kale is clearly the point of the dish, and a warm oven snack suits the weather.

plain_voice.reason: Clear, friendly British English with useful reasons given, such as drying the leaves so they crisp rather than steam.

hearty_healthy.reason: A vegetable-based snack with seeds and cheese that children would happily eat, with no sugar or refined starch.
